briarwatch-square.act: Act I — A Village Holding Its Breath
briarwatch-square.title: The Silent Bell
briarwatch-square.objective: Learn why the ward-bell fell silent, then follow Tovin's trail into the Briarwood.

lines.narrate: Rain beads on a bell rope cut cleanly at shoulder height. Above the square, Briarwatch's ward-bell hangs mute for the first time in living memory. Without it, nothing rings back the Gloam: the cold mist from the old places that takes the warmth out of a house, and then the names out of the people in it.
Reeve Aveline stands under the inn's awning with a wax tablet, ticking off shuttered windows.

lines.text: Forty-one households. Thirty-eight have answered their door. The other three are the Pellows, who never answer, and two I am trying not to think about.
When did you last sleep?
Before this. Ask me something useful, Stoneward.
The fog on the north road. Was it there yesterday?
No. And you knew that, Sister. You were looking straight at it when you asked.

lines.narrate: Across the square, the forge is the only lit doorway. Smith Dera has propped it open, as if to tell the whole village that somebody here is still working.

briarwatch-square.revisit: Back in the square the rain has not let up. The bell still hangs silent, Aveline is still counting doors, and the forge is still the only lit doorway.

choices.label: Inspect the severed bell rope
choices.description: Examine the cut, residue, and nearby tower fittings.

lines.narrate: Under the rain-dark fibres you find a thumbprint of black wax, stamped with a thorn wound around a broken bell.

lines.text: That's a seal, not a thief's mark. Somebody wanted it found, or didn't care if it was.
Or never thought anyone would look this closely.

lines.narrate: The rain has ruined most of the traces. Maren takes the rope's end from you and turns it to the light.

lines.text: Look at the fray. The bell stopped first. Somebody cut the rope afterwards.
So the cut didn't silence it.
No. The cut was so nobody could ring it again.

choices.label: Question Reeve Aveline
choices.description: Read what the reeve is reluctant to say about the bell-keeper and Warden Sable.

lines.text: Warden Sable came to see Tovin two nights ago. In the bell tower, after dark, which is not where anyone discusses the weather.
They argued. I heard Tovin say "not like this". Sable rode north before dawn, and nobody has seen him since.
You told the village it was a broken clapper.
I told the village to go to bed. It was the only order I was sure they'd follow.

lines.narrate: Aveline gives the account she has given all morning: a broken clapper, a smith sent for, nothing to fear.
Each time Sable's name comes up, her eyes go to the infirmary window.

lines.text: Whatever she isn't saying, Tovin knows it.

choices.label: Stop at Dera's forge
choices.description: The smith has been working with her door open all morning. She notices things.

choices.label: Visit the wounded bell-keeper
choices.description: Tovin survived the night but has not spoken coherently since returning from the wood.

choices.label: Follow the north road into the Briarwood
choices.description: Commit to the trail. More evidence may make later choices easier.

dera-forge.act: Act I — A Village Holding Its Breath
dera-forge.title: The Only Lit Doorway
dera-forge.objective: Hear what the smith saw while the rest of the village stayed indoors.

lines.narrate: The forge is warm enough to steam the rain off your cloak. Dera is filing the edge of a hinge that does not need filing.

lines.text: If you've come about the bell, you pay like everyone else. What are they saying at the inn?
That it's a broken clapper.
It isn't. I made that clapper. I would know.

Here's what I have. Last week Tovin brought me a lantern to mend. Black glass, no wick, cold as a well bucket. He said Warden Sable gave it to him and he wanted to know what it was for. I couldn't tell him.
Do you still have it?
He came back for it the day before he went into the wood. Took it north with him.

choices.label: Pay her in gossip
choices.description: Tell Dera something she doesn't already know, if you can.

lines.narrate: You tell her the Pellows have not answered their door all morning.

lines.text: The Pellows never answer their door. That's not gossip, that's weather.
Fine. One thing more, because you mended my roof in spring and only fell off it once. The fog on the north road doesn't move with the wind. I've watched it all morning. It moves toward us.

choices.label: Ask her to keep the forge lit tonight
choices.description: A lit doorway might matter more than she lets on.

lines.text: I was going to anyway. Somebody should look like they aren't afraid.
Are you?
Ask me when you're back.

choices.label: Thank her and go back to the square
choices.description: Leave her to her hinge.

lines.text: Bring the bell-keeper back in one piece. I'm not making a second clapper for nobody to ring.

tovin-infirmary.act: Act I — A Village Holding Its Breath
tovin-infirmary.title: A Witness Who Hears the Bell
tovin-infirmary.objective: Learn what Tovin encountered without breaking what remains of his composure.

lines.narrate: Tovin lies under three wool blankets, one hand closed around a rope that isn't there. Each time thunder rolls he whispers a line that nearly becomes a prayer.
Maren kneels a little way from the bed, close enough to be seen and not so close she crowds him. Orin shuts the door and stands with his back to it.

lines.text: Is it ringing? I keep hearing it ring.
It isn't, Tovin. Do you know where you are?
Infirmary. Third bed. The one with the short leg.

lines.narrate: He tries to smile. It goes wrong halfway.

tovin-infirmary.revisit: Tovin has turned onto his side. Maren checks his bandage without waking him.

choices.label: Calm Tovin and let him set the pace
choices.description: Use patience and reassurance to separate memory from panic.

lines.narrate: You sit, and wait, and let the rain do the talking for a while.

lines.text: They had a verse. Sable's people. "Name the grief, then ring it home." They said it at the old shrine and the roots opened like a door.
I said it too. I don't know why I said it.
Because you were frightened and they were sure. That isn't the same as agreeing with them.

lines.narrate: Tovin gets as far as "name the grief" and stops, breathing hard.
Instead he draws in the dust on the bedside table with one finger: an arch, two pillars, a broken stone laid across the top.

lines.text: The old shrine on the north road.

choices.label: Examine the wound on Tovin's shoulder
choices.description: Determine what dragged or marked him in the wood.

lines.narrate: Under the bandage the wound is clean-edged and packed with grey ash. The barbs that made it were cut in repeating threes.

lines.text: Not teeth. A briar hook, the kind we bless at harvest. Somebody blessed this one for something else.

lines.narrate: You clean the wound and bind it fresh, but you cannot tell what made it.

lines.text: North. It was north.

lines.narrate: His breathing steadies, and for a moment he looks like the man who rang the bell every evening at six.

choices.label: Press Tovin for an immediate answer
choices.description: Use fear and urgency. This may produce information at a human cost.

lines.narrate: You lean over the bed and ask again, harder.

lines.text: "Name the grief, then ring it home." The shrine's on the north road past the split oak. Please. Please stop.

lines.narrate: He turns his face to the wall.

lines.text: We have it. That's enough.

lines.narrate: Tovin's breath goes ragged and he tries to climb out of the bed.

lines.text: Out. Both of you. Now.

lines.narrate: It is several minutes before she lets you back in, and she does not look at you when she does.

choices.label: Return to the village square
choices.description: Rejoin Reeve Aveline and prepare to leave.

forest-edge.title: Three Ways into the Briarwood
forest-edge.objective: Choose a route toward the hidden hollow and accept the risks that come with it.
forest-edge.opening: The north road divides beneath trees knitted together by old thorns. Wagon ruts vanish into fern on the left. A pilgrim marker leans toward a narrow rise. From the misted hollow to the right comes one faint, impossible bell note.

choices.label: Track the missing wagon through the fern
choices.description: Use spoor and broken vegetation to approach the ambushers on better terms.

success.text: Nessa's kind of trailcraft would approve: you find the ambush line before it closes and turn the trap back on its makers.

failure.text: The trail is deliberately doubled. A cord snaps behind you and masked figures rise from the brush.

choices.label: Take the old pilgrim path
choices.description: Follow weathered ward-stones toward the shrine Tovin remembered.
choices.lockedText: You have not learned enough to identify the pilgrim path with confidence.

success.text: The old marks resolve into a sequence of safe steps. The path carries you above the traps and toward a forgotten shrine.

failure.text: You find the shrine, but a false ward-stone cuts the party with a burst of thorn splinters.

choices.label: Follow the impossible bell-note into the mist
choices.description: Trust instinct and the sound no one in the village could hear.

success.text: You separate the true note from its echoes and discover a trapped Briarwatch scout before the hunters return.

failure.text: The note leads in circles. By the time you find the snare clearing, the creatures guarding it are already moving.

choices.label: Advance openly along the main road
choices.description: Fast and direct, but the route offers little concealment.

old-shrine.title: The Shrine of the First Answer
old-shrine.objective: Recover the shrine's forgotten knowledge and find the under-road into the cult's hollow.
old-shrine.opening: Roots split the shrine's roof but leave its little silver bell untouched. Six names have been chiselled from the altar. A seventh remains beneath soot, beside a stone reliquary with no visible hinge.

choices.label: Reconstruct the erased dedication
choices.description: Compare the surviving script, Tovin's verse, and the bell's old iconography.

success.text: The missing dedication names the bell Aster Vey—‘the star that answers.’ The silver chime rings once when you speak it aloud.

failure.text: The full name escapes you, but the surviving vow makes one fact clear: the ward-spirit once answered willing keepers, not masters.

choices.label: Open the seamless stone reliquary
choices.description: Search for the concealed catch or work the seal with proper tools.

success.text: A hidden pin yields. Inside are two flasks of holy water and a travel cloak woven with living-looking briars.

failure.text: The catch bites like a thorn. The reliquary opens, but its ward burns your hand before fading.

choices.label: Descend into the root-lined under-road
choices.description: Leave the shrine through the passage beneath its altar.

mist-hollow.title: The Snared Scout
mist-hollow.objective: Free the trapped scout before the briar wolves close in.

lines.narrate: A young scout hangs upside down above a carpet of thorn roots, one boot caught in a wire snare, her hair brushing the briars. Beyond the fog two low shapes pace and stop, pace and stop.

lines.text: Don't. Don't come closer, that's a trigger line, the whole hollow's strung with them.
We'll get you down.
I know you'll get me down, I'm asking you to get me down quietly, which is a different...
Then we wait for the wolves to move off.
I have been waiting. I have been waiting for an hour. All of my blood is in my head.
What's your name?
Nessa. Nessa Reed. Can we do names after?

choices.label: Disarm the snare without alerting the wolves
choices.description: Use careful hands and the scout's whispered directions.

lines.narrate: The wire slackens without a sound. Nessa drops, and Orin catches her before anyone has to ask.

lines.text: Put me down.
You'll fall over.

lines.narrate: She sits down hard in the bracken, swears, and is on her feet again before he can help. Then she leads you through a gap in the wolves' patrol, limping, without once looking back to see if you're following.
The catch gives with a bright metallic snap. Nessa lands on her shoulder among the roots.

lines.text: That was the loud way.

lines.narrate: Beyond the fog, the wolves stop pacing.

choices.label: Have Orin hold the wolves while you cut Nessa free
choices.description: A companion-led plan: Orin becomes the obvious target while you work quickly.

lines.text: Cut her down. I'll be the noisy one.

lines.narrate: He walks into the open and hammers his shield three times. Both wolves turn toward the sound.

lines.text: Is he always like this?
Yes.

choices.label: Rush the snare and cut it by force
choices.description: Fast, loud, and physically demanding.

lines.narrate: You tear the anchor out of the ground and drag Nessa clear before the wolves cross the clearing.

lines.text: That's one way to do it.

lines.narrate: The thorn-root holds. Nessa pulls a knife from her boot, saws through her own snare and drops hard, just as the pack reaches you.

mist-hollow-after.title: What Nessa Saw
mist-hollow-after.objective: Hear Nessa's report and choose the route to the hidden gate.

lines.narrate: Nessa binds her ankle with a strip of her own sleeve and draws the hollow in the mud from memory.

lines.text: I followed Warden Sable. Three nights. There's a root-gate under the ridge, here. He had a black seal and he talked to the ground.
And the ground answered.
You followed a warden into the Briarwood alone.
Somebody had to. You weren't here.
Who taught you to track like that?
Somebody who isn't here either.

choices.label: Ask Nessa what the bell sounded like
choices.description: Her answer may distinguish a monster from a bound spirit.

lines.text: It didn't sound hungry. It sounded like somebody crying who doesn't want you to hear.
Then it isn't a monster. It's a spirit, and someone is forcing it through a rite that was never meant for it.
I don't know. I don't want to think about the sound. I know it was Sable giving the orders, though. I'd know his voice anywhere now.

choices.label: Let Nessa guide the party to the root-gate
choices.description: Take the scout's concealed ridge path.

ambush-aftermath.title: The Mask Comes Off
ambush-aftermath.objective: Search the ambush site and decide what to do with the wounded lookout.
ambush-aftermath.opening: The last goblin flees into the fern. A wounded cult lookout lies beside a dropped satchel, mask cracked, one hand held away from her spear. The black seal recovered from the fight is still warm.

choices.label: Search the lookout's satchel
choices.description: Look for orders, maps, and proof of who funded the ambush.

success.text: A false seam hides a cipher strip bearing Sable's crest and a route to the root-gate.

failure.text: You find the route marks but miss whatever the lookout tried hardest to conceal.

choices.label: Offer the wounded lookout mercy for the truth
choices.description: Promise treatment and a fair hearing in exchange for useful information.

success.text: She gives her name—Lysa—and admits Sable changed the binding rite. The spirit below is a prisoner, not an ally. She marks a safe sign on the root-gate.

failure.text: Lysa refuses to give names, but she lets Maren treat her. Before she limps into the fern she looks back once: ‘The bell remembers who betrayed it.’

choices.label: Threaten the lookout with the road's consequences
choices.description: Force directions quickly, risking the party's trust.

success.text: Lysa gives the route and Sable's hand-sign, then crawls away when released.

failure.text: She calls your bluff and spits in the fern. Orin takes the map from the fallen satchel, and Lysa is gone into the trees before anyone thinks to stop her.

choices.label: Follow the route toward the hidden root-gate
choices.description: Leave the ambush site and enter the old underways.

underroad.title: The Flooded Under-Road
underroad.objective: Cross the drowned passage without arriving exhausted or exposed.
underroad.opening: Black water fills the old pilgrim tunnel from wall to wall. Bell-shaped niches mark a path beneath the surface, but the current pulls toward a shaft where something large turns slowly below.

choices.label: Rig a rope line across the current
choices.description: Use fifty feet of rope to give the whole party a secure crossing.

result.text: The rope holds. One by one the party crosses while Orin anchors the line and you watch the dark shaft.

choices.label: Read the submerged pilgrim markers
choices.description: Find the old stepping route beneath the water.

success.text: The niches align with a raised spine of stone. The party crosses with wet boots and no worse.

failure.text: A false step drops everyone waist-deep into the current. Packs stay closed, but the cold takes its toll.

choices.label: Wade through and hold the weaker swimmers
choices.description: Rely on raw strength and endurance.

success.text: You break the current's line and create a moving shield for the others.

failure.text: The current slams the party against the stone lip before Orin drags everyone clear.

root-gate.title: The Door That Drinks Names
root-gate.objective: Open the cult's gate without surrendering the advantage.
root-gate.opening: A door grown from black roots seals the passage. Its bronze mouth bears no keyhole, only a shallow seal-mark and a line of script: WHAT ENTERS UNNAMED ENTERS OWNED.

choices.label: Press the black-wax cult seal into the bronze mouth
choices.description: Use the conspirators' own sign to enter as expected guests.

result.text: The roots taste the seal and draw aside. Beyond, cultists continue their work, unaware that the wrong party has entered.

choices.label: Answer the gate with the bell's true name
choices.description: Invoke Aster Vey and reject the gate's claim of ownership.

result.text: At the name Aster Vey, silver light travels through the roots. The door opens and the distant wraith answers with a note of recognition.

choices.label: Find and work the living lock
choices.description: Use tools and patience to separate the root tendons around the latch.

success.text: The lock opens without a cry. Nessa catches the door before its bronze teeth can ring together.

failure.text: The root-lock shrieks like metal under strain. The door opens, but the court beyond is ready.

choices.label: Break the root-gate by force
choices.description: Destroy the barrier before it can close around you.

success.text: The bronze mouth splits under a final blow. Every voice beyond falls silent.

failure.text: The roots recoil and lash back before the weakened gate gives way.

hollow-court.title: The Hollow Court
hollow-court.objective: Reach the bell-vault and obtain proof of Sable's role if possible.
hollow-court.opening: The hollow court was once a wardens' hall. Now roots pin old shields to the walls. Acolytes carry bronze bowls between a cipher desk and a stair descending toward the bell-vault.

choices.label: Eavesdrop on the acolytes at the cipher desk
choices.description: Learn the ritual sequence and where Sable keeps his orders.

success.text: You hear that Sable altered the final verse and keeps the payment ledger beneath the desk's false bottom.

failure.text: A censer stops mid-swing. The acolyte looks directly toward your hiding place and calls the guards.

choices.label: Let Nessa steal the ledger while the party creates a distraction
choices.description: A companion-led plan that depends on the rescued scout.

success.text: Orin begins a loud argument about delivery seals. Nessa slips behind the desk and returns with the ledger before the acolyte finishes objecting.

failure.text: The false bottom catches. Nessa gets the ledger, but the desk's bronze alarm rings through the court.

choices.label: Challenge the court and break through
choices.description: Abandon subtlety and clear the route by force.

choices.label: Use Lysa's safe sign to pass the court
choices.description: Trust the spared lookout's mark and walk through as defectors expected by the cult.

success.text: The sentries return the sign. You pass beneath their eyes and reach the vault stairs without drawing steel.

failure.text: One sentry knows the sign should be mirrored. His hand closes around the alarm chain.

vault-antechamber.title: Plans Before the Last Door
vault-antechamber.objective: Choose how the party will disrupt Sable's ritual before entering the bell-vault.
vault-antechamber.opening: The last door trembles with each slow toll from below. Through its seams you see Sable at a circle of black candles and the outline of a chained spirit inside the cracked bell. Your companions speak in low voices; each has a different answer.

choices.label: Follow Maren's plan: restore the original warding verse
choices.description: Use the true name or binding evidence to turn the ritual against Sable.

success.text: Maren rebuilds the missing line and the vault answers. The spirit's chains become visible—and breakable.

failure.text: The verse catches but does not hold. It weakens the binding enough to deny the wraith some of Sable's protection.

choices.label: Follow Orin's plan: collapse the chain winch
choices.description: Destroy the mechanism feeding tension into the spirit's binding.

success.text: Orin wedges his shield into the winch and tears its axle free. The ritual circle lurches out of alignment.

failure.text: The axle bends but holds. Orin leaves it one blow from failure and readies his shield.

choices.label: Follow Nessa's plan: steal Sable's binding key
choices.description: Slip through the service slit and take the bronze key from Sable's belt.

success.text: Nessa returns with the bronze key and Sable's expression changes from certainty to fear.

failure.text: Sable turns at the last instant. Nessa escapes with a cut sleeve and the knowledge that surprise is gone.

choices.label: Enter together and confront Sable with what you know
choices.description: Rely on accumulated evidence, presence, and the party's united front.

bell-vault.title: The Bell Beneath Briarwatch
bell-vault.objective: Break Sable's control of the ward-spirit and survive the final reckoning.
bell-vault.opening: The buried bell is larger than the village tower above it. Black roots suspend it over a pit of pale fire. Warden Sable stands inside the ritual circle with one hand on a bronze chain. A human shape presses against the bell's inner surface each time it tolls.

choices.label: Ring the silver chime and name Aster Vey
choices.description: Call the ward-spirit home through its true name rather than Sable's binding.

success.text: The silver chime cuts through the black toll. The spirit turns from you to Sable and the binding burns away from its wrists.

failure.text: The spirit hears its name but cannot reach it through the altered verse. Its resistance still tears gaps in Sable's protection.

choices.label: Expose Sable with the cipher ledger
choices.description: Turn his followers against him before the ritual completes.

success.text: The ledger passes from hand to shaking hand. Two acolytes cut the secondary chains and flee; Sable loses control of the circle.

failure.text: Sable calls the ledger a forgery and orders the final toll. Doubt remains in the room, but not enough to stop him.

choices.label: Turn the stolen binding key against the ritual
choices.description: Release the primary chain using Sable's own key.

result.text: The key turns once. Every chain but Sable's personal tether falls away, leaving the spirit free to resist him.

choices.label: Break the ritual by force
choices.description: Enter combat before the next toll. Prior preparations still affect the encounter.

ending.title: When the Bell Answers
ending.objective: The chapter is complete. Review the consequences of your choices.
ending.opening: Dawn reaches Briarwatch before the party does. The ward-bell sounds once across the wet roofs—not as an alarm, but as an answer. Villagers step into the road while your companions carry the proof, the wounded, and the names of those who did not return.

choices.label: Conclude the chapter
choices.description: Record the ending and leave the party ready for a future campaign chapter.

result.text: Briarwatch begins the work of choosing new wardens. Your party's bonds—and its disagreements—will follow you beyond the village.

defeat.title: The Bell Keeps Tolling
defeat.location: A Memory of the Last Stand
defeat.objective: Reload a save or begin a new campaign.
defeat.opening: The party falls before the ward can be restored. Briarwatch's bell continues beneath the earth, each toll carrying Sable's command farther through the roots.
